title: My Ideal Healthy Meal Plan
writingModel: My Ideal Healthy Meal Plan — by Zhibek Akhmetova

As a volleyball player and a student, I need a lot of energy throughout the day. My meal plan is designed around three goals: enough protein to support my training, enough variety to keep me interested, and not too much processed food. Here is what a typical day looks like for me.

Breakfast should be substantial. I usually have a bowl of porridge with a little honey and a few walnuts. I add a small amount of milk — not too much, as I don't want it to be too heavy before a morning lecture. I also drink a large glass of water and sometimes a cup of green tea with a little sugar. I need enough energy to last until lunchtime without snacking too much.

For lunch, I try to have a lot of vegetables — usually a portion of roasted or steamed vegetables — and a moderate amount of protein: chicken, lentils, or eggs. I don't eat too many carbohydrates at lunch because I find I feel sleepy in afternoon lectures. I eat enough to feel full, but not so much that I feel heavy.

Dinner is my main meal. I cook enough food for two days — this saves a lot of time during the week. I like rice or pasta with a generous portion of vegetables and a small amount of meat. I don't add too much oil or sauce — I prefer lighter food in the evening. I drink plenty of water with dinner and sometimes a small glass of kefir.

Snacks are important for an athlete. I keep a few pieces of fruit in my room and sometimes some nuts — a small handful is enough. I try not to eat too many biscuits or crisps, even though I enjoy them. I allow myself a small amount of chocolate once or twice a week as a reward after training.

My shopping list is simple. Each week I buy enough rice or pasta for five days, a dozen eggs, a few tins of lentils, plenty of vegetables, and a small amount of meat. The total usually comes to about 9,000-10,000 tenge. Not a lot of money, but enough to eat really well.
